text_blocks.snippet: Recent scam warnings across Central Illinois highlight a rise in sophisticated phone, AI voice, and impersonation schemes.
snippet_highlighted_words: sophisticated phone, AI voice, and impersonation schemes

list.snippet: Law Enforcement & Government Impersonation: Scammers spoof phone numbers (such as Springfield area codes or local sheriff's offices) to pose as the Illinois State Police, the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Central District of Illinois, or local county sheriffs. They claim you missed jury duty, have a pension issue, or face a warrant, demanding immediate money or gift cards.

AI-Generated Voice & Romance Scams: Reported heavily in areas like Peoria County, scammers use artificial intelligence-generated voices and fake online personas to build trust over time before requesting money or financial information.

Bank Impersonation Calls: Community banks—including Fisher National Bank and Federated Bank—have warned customers of fake callers displaying the bank’s actual name or phone number on caller ID to steal login details.
Secretary of State Smishing: Fraudulent text messages falsely claim to be from the Illinois Secretary of State, threatening license suspensions and demanding payment or personal data.
Home Repair & Storm Chasers: Door-to-door contractors and storm-chasing crews target homeowners with high-pressure tactics, demands for large cash advances, or substandard/incomplete work.
Hang up immediately: Legitimate government agencies, courts, and banks will never cold-call you demanding cash, cryptocurrency, or sensitive login credentials.
Verify independently: Do not trust caller ID. Look up the official phone number of your bank or local agency independently and call them back directly.
Never click text links: Do not tap links in unexpected text messages claiming to be from state offices like the Illinois Secretary of State.
